findings.issue_text: packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73 — P1 confidence 100: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` selects the organizer's calendar for every co-host credential, so collective bookings with distinct Office365 destination IDs target an inaccessible or incorrect calendar instead of each co-host's destination; the same unchanged one-argument adapter contract and first-element selection occur in packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128 and packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:170 — P1 confidence 100: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined,` drops the credential ID from every newly created video reference, so cancellation skips deleting the remote video meeting because handleCancelBooking.ts:491 requires `bookingVideoReference.credentialId`.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:148 — P1 confidence 100: `(cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId` never selects a legacy destination whose credentialId is null, so the explicitly supported integration-based fallback in EventManager.ts:376 creates that booking on `primary` rather than its configured secondary calendar.

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:317 — P1 confidence 100: `: event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` compares stored calendar IDs to a missing externalCalendarId precisely when the fallback executes, so callers without a reference calendar ID delete from primary instead of the configured secondary calendar; updateEvent repeats the same broken fallback at line 256.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:555 — P1 confidence 75: `const oldCalendarEvent = booking.references.find((reference) => reference.type.includes("_calendar"));` deletes only one old remote event when a collective booking is merged into another booking via newBookingId, leaving the other co-host calendar events active after all destination references have been updated.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:344 — P2 confidence 100 advisory: `const credentialFromDB = await prisma.credential.findUnique({` inside the destination loop adds one serial database round trip per co-host whose credential is absent from the organizer's credentials, increasing collective-booking latency with host count; small teams limit the impact but do not remove the N+1 path, and fetching all missing IDs with one findMany removes the per-host query.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:355 — P2 confidence 100 advisory: `if (credentialFromDB && credentialFromDB.app?.slug) {` and its credential reconstruction are duplicated in creation and updating while cancellation uses a third resolver without that guard, so credentials lacking app metadata are treated differently across booking lifecycle operations and future resolver changes require three edits; local self-containment is the strongest justification but does not resolve the existing policy drift, and a shared credential resolver removes both duplicated reconstruction blocks.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/confirm.handler.ts:175 — [P1, confidence 100] `destinationCalendar: booking?.destinationCalendar ? [booking.destinationCalendar] : user.destinationCalendar ? [user.destinationCalendar] : []` reconstructs only the organizer destination when a collective booking is confirmed, so the other hosts never receive calendar events; the same singleton reconstruction in both payment webhooks leaves paid collective bookings outside the multiple-host fix because initial booking creation defers calendar creation for confirmation and payment.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:119 — P1 confidence 100: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` throws TypeError when Google Meet is selected with an empty or null destinationCalendar, aborting booking creation after its database record is saved instead of applying the existing Cal Video fallback.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:170 — P1 confidence 100: `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined` discards the credential ID for newly created video meetings, so handleCancelBooking.ts:490 skips `if (bookingVideoReference && bookingVideoReference.credentialId)` and reports successful cancellation while leaving the remote video meeting active.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:449 — P1 confidence 100: `const promises = bookingToDelete.user.credentials` inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` repeats organizer-only deletions for every collective reference when allRemainingBookings is true, while `updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))` selects only the first host's event, leaving cohosts' recurring events active despite a successful cancellation response.

packages/core/EventManager.ts:356 — Advisory P2 confidence 75: `if (credentialFromDB && credentialFromDB.app?.slug)` followed by `if (credential)` silently omits a cohost's calendar when the newly introduced database lookup returns no usable credential, so booking consumers receive no failed result or warning; tolerating disconnected integrations is the strongest rebuttal, but toleration does not justify reporting only the other hosts' successes and hiding the skipped host from appsStatus.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151 — [P1, confidence 100] The unrelated organization-creation change `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}),` reverses the existing billing condition, so installations with team billing disabled now create organizations without their requested slug even after configuring that slug as a subdomain, an organization-provisioning regression outside the collective-host destination-calendar task.

apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:249 — P2 confidence 100 advisory: the sole changed test asserts `destinationCalendar: []` for a single-user rejected booking, so deleting the new second-host creation/update/cancellation behavior leaves this test green and collective hosts lose regression protection; although this correctly verifies empty-array webhook serialization, that assertion never exercises two destinations or checks either host’s remote calendar side effects.

goldens.comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.

Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled

The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
